terms.gloss: town hall; classically a council house
evidence: M-O s.v. city hall, town hall
terms.comment: The house where a council met: at Rome the senate house, and the council houses of other towns too, such as the one at Syracuse that its people called the bouleuterion (Cic. Verr. 2.2.50; Lewis & Short). Traupman gives it for a city hall; Morgan–Owens for a city or town hall, as Vives used it of the house where the magistrates of Valencia met.

terms.grammar: noun phrase: cūria with the adjective mūnicipālis
evidence: M-O s.v. city hall, town hall
terms.comment: Mūnicipālis, of a mūnicipium, a self-governing town, is classical (Cic., Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: effundī in vestibulō cūriae jussit ānulōs aureōs
phrases.english: he had the gold rings tipped out in the entrance of the council house (at Carthage)

sources: Lewis & Short: curia · Lewis & Short: municipalis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. city hall, town hall; legislature: building in which a legislature or municipal council convenes.
